en: The 1 June notice covers June incentives: BTC/BONK trading-fee discounts and partial liquidation rebates on eligible non-BTC markets. Gas, bridging, slippage and third-party costs remain. It establishes no September renewal, so the reviewed June period is historical.

The July update distinguishes the new Arcus product from dYdX v4 and says v4 continues to be supported. A possible future token allocation is mentioned without a claim amount or date. Neither this notice nor a historical campaign proves a current signup reward.

The 4 September notice describes CPUSDT perpetuals in the Innovation Zone, settled in USDT with four-hour funding. Innovation Zone fees are higher; listing parameters can change. It does not establish spot availability or personal eligibility.

The 4 September notice adds AVA, GNS, SCR and TOWNS to Monitoring Tags, identifying possible delisting risk. The UK page warns that some named tokens may not be available there; this is a monitoring notice, not a new listing or reward.
This dated Europe campaign ends at 00:00 UTC on 7 September. The first-200 new-user deposit/trade tasks award fee-rebate vouchers, not cash; higher tiers have distinct terms.
The inviter's $10,000 volume requirement and fee share are separate from the referred user's benefit. Region and identity requirements are not specified on this page.
A valid referral code or link must be applied. This research panel does not include referral codes; the sign-up cards on this site do and disclose the commission.
The reviewed Drift notice discusses recovery of outstanding user losses and a protocol reboot. It does not verify normal current trading or deposit availability.
The reviewed dYdX incentive notice covers June, while a later product update distinguishes Arcus from dYdX v4. Neither establishes a current signup payout.
